title: First week for a new engineer
description: What the first week actually looks like, including the parts where you are stuck waiting for an account.

states.name: Offer accepted
states.description: You have signed, but you do not start yet. Someone on the team is quietly ordering hardware and filing access requests on your behalf.

states.name: Hardware on the way
states.description: A laptop is being provisioned and shipped. Your accounts exist on paper but none of them work yet.
states.annotation: If nothing has arrived two days before your start date, say so early. Shipping is the most common cause of a lost first day.

states.name: Day one setup
states.description: You are working through the setup checklist: sign in to mail and chat, pull the main repository, and install the toolchain.

states.name: Blocked on an account
states.description: One system will not let you in. You cannot finish setup, and it is not obvious whether the request was never filed or simply not approved.

states.name: Ask your onboarding buddy
states.description: You are asking the person assigned to you rather than guessing. They have seen this failure before and know which queue the request is sitting in.
states.annotation: Asking after twenty minutes of being stuck is normal here, not a sign you are struggling.

states.name: Meet the team
states.description: Short introductions with the people you will work with. You are learning who owns what, and who to ask when something breaks.

states.name: Read the team docs
states.description: You are reading the architecture overview and the on-call runbook, mostly to build a map rather than to memorise anything.

states.name: Run the service locally
states.description: You are getting the service and its test suite running on your own machine. This is the first real signal that your setup is complete.

states.name: Pick up a first task
states.description: You have a small, well-scoped ticket chosen to touch the build, the tests and the review process rather than to be useful.

states.name: Open a pull request
states.description: Your change is up for review. The point is to exercise the pipeline end to end and to meet your reviewers.

states.name: Address review comments
states.description: A reviewer left comments. You are separating the ones that change behaviour from the ones about house style, and answering both.

states.name: First week retro
states.description: You shipped something small and you know how the work flows. You are writing down every place the onboarding docs were wrong while you can still see it.
states.annotation: A new joiner is the only person who can see the gaps in onboarding. Fix the docs now; in a month you will not notice them.

states.name: Hand it to your manager
states.description: The blocker is organisational rather than technical, and it is not yours to solve. Your manager takes it from here while you work on something else.

transitions.label: IT fixed it within the hour
Still blocked after a full day
You know what the team owns
The build fails only on your machine
transitions.description: A setup problem, not a code problem. Someone has hit it before.

transitions.label: The task turned out to be much larger
